- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?
With calculate_per_token_loss=True and a Python-int token count, TopKRouter.attach_and_log_load_balancing_loss builds the aux-loss token count with torch.tensor(num_local_tokens, device=...). That copies from pageable host memory, which CUDA graph capture forbids, so per-layer CUDA graphs that include moe_router stop at capture with seq_aux_loss and global_aux_loss (a regression from #7046). Fill the count on the device with torch.full instead; the value, dtype and shape are unchanged.

Add TestPerTokenAuxLossCudaGraph, which captures and replays the router with per-token loss for both load-balancing types.

:warning: For major changes (either in lines of code or in its impact), please make sure to first share a design doc with the team. If you're unsure what's the best way to do so, contact @NVIDIA/mcore-oncall.

- **New features**: a linked issue is **required**. Please open a [feature request](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/issues/new?template=feature_request.md) and reference it here before submitting the PR.
- **Small updates (bug fixes, minor improvements)**: a linked issue is **recommended** and will accelerate the PR review process.

Linked issue: <!-- e.g. Fixes #1234 / Related to #1234 -->

- [x] I have added relevant unit tests
- [x] I have added relevant functional tests
- [ ] If this PR adds or changes a GPU kernel (Triton, `jit_fuser`/`torch.compile`, CUDA extension, TE or external-library dispatch, or a scatter/index accumulation), I have added or updated its bit-exact determinism test and registered it in `tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/manifest.py` ([guide](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/docs/developer/determinism/testing.md))
- [ ] I have added proper typing to my code [Typing guidelines](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html)
- [ ] I have added relevant documentation
- [ ] I have run the [autoformatter.sh](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/tools/autoformat.sh) on my PR

### Code review

Feel free to message or comment @NVIDIA/mcore-oncall to help accelerate your merge into main. The less complex your PR is, the faster it will be approved and merged!

All PRs start as **draft**. If you open a non-draft PR, it will be automatically converted to draft.

#### Step 1: Mark PR as "Ready for Review"

files.patch:
@@ -457,6 +457,33 @@ def test_topk_router_replays(self, balancing, score, expert_bias, hash_routing):
             what=f"TopKRouter[{balancing}, hash={hash_routing}]",
         )
 
+    # aux_loss passes its already-reduced token count; these two build the count from the local
+    # token dimension.
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("balancing", ["seq_aux_loss", "global_aux_loss"])
+    def test_topk_router_per_token_aux_loss_replays(self, balancing):
+        """With per-token loss the router scales the aux loss by the token count summed over TP
+        and CP ranks. Without a padding mask the local count is a Python int, which the router
+        fills into a device tensor before the all-reduce."""
+        self._init()
+        seeded()
+        config = _moe_config(
+            num_moe_experts=64,
+            moe_router_topk=8,
+            moe_router_load_balancing_type=balancing,
+            calculate_per_token_loss=True,
+        )
+        router = TopKRouter(
+            config, pg_collection=ProcessGroupCollection.use_mpu_process_groups()
+        ).cuda()
+        router.set_layer_number(0)
+        hidden = torch.randn(2048, 4, 1024, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16, requires_grad=True)
+        # global_aux_loss averages the token counts of every call so far, and the harness does
+        # not reset that buffer; with identical inputs the average is the same in every replay.
+        assert_module_replays_bit_exact(
+            router, (hidden,), replays=3, what=f"TopKRouter[{balancing}, per-token loss]"
+        )
+        moe_utils.get_moe_metrics_tracker().clear()
+
     @pytest.mark.skipif(
         not (HAVE_TE_ROUTER and moe_utils.fused_topk_with_score_function_supports_topk_indices),
         reason="TE dense fused router output is not available",

@@ -502,6 +502,63 @@ def test_runtime_group_aux_loss_gradient_scaling(self, runtime_cp_size):
         torch.testing.assert_close(aux_source.grad, expected_grad)
 
 
+class TestPerTokenAuxLossCudaGraph:
+    """Per-token aux-loss scaling must stay capturable: per-layer CUDA graphs capture the router."""
+
+    def setup_method(self, method):
+        Utils.initialize_model_parallel(1, 1)
+        _set_random_seed(seed_=123, data_parallel_random_init=False)
+
+    def teardown_method(self, method):
+        MoEAuxLossAutoScaler.main_loss_backward_scale = None
+        Utils.destroy_model_parallel()
+
+    @pytest.mark.internal
+    @pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="CUDA not available")
+    # aux_loss passes its already-reduced token count; these two build the count from the local
+    # token dimension.
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("load_balancing_type", ["seq_aux_loss", "global_aux_loss"])
+    def test_router_forward_is_capturable(self, load_balancing_type):
+        config = TransformerConfig(
+            num_layers=2,
+            hidden_size=12,
+            num_attention_heads=4,
+            num_moe_experts=4,
+            use_cpu_initialization=True,
+            moe_router_load_balancing_type=load_balancing_type,
+            moe_router_topk=2,
+            moe_aux_loss_coeff=1.0,
+            calculate_per_token_loss=True,
+            add_bias_linear=False,
+        )
+        submodules = get_submodules(
+            get_gpt_layer_local_submodules(num_experts=4, moe_grouped_gemm=False).mlp
+        )
+        assert isinstance(submodules, MoESubmodules)
+        router = cast(TopKRouter, MoELayer(config, submodules).router).cuda().train()
+        hidden_states = torch.randn(8, 2, config.hidden_size, device="cuda")
+
+        warmup_stream = torch.cuda.Stream()
+        warmup_stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
+        with torch.cuda.stream(warmup_stream):
+            for _ in range(2):
+                router(hidden_states)
+        torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(warmup_stream)
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+
+        # Without padding the aux-loss token count is a Python int from the static token
+        # dimension. Building it with a host-to-device copy fails during capture.
+        graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+        with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+            probs, routing_map = router(hidden_states)
+        graph.replay()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+
+        num_tokens = hidden_states.shape[0] * hidden_states.shape[1]
+        assert torch.isfinite(probs).all()
+        assert routing_map.sum().item() == num_tokens * config.moe_router_topk
+
+
 class TestTop2Router:
     def setup_method(self, method):
         Utils.initialize_model_parallel(1, 1)

<!-- nemo-ci-review-impact:v1 ceiling=none -->

Strict review passed: no significant issues found. LGTM.

**Findings:** CRITICAL: 0, IMPORTANT: 0, SUGGESTION: 0

**What I checked**

- **Production change** ([router.py#L793-L798](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/4cda138c49a84c400e1af305c551f8e243ff2664/megatron/core/transformer/moe/router.py#L793-L798)). The old code was `torch.tensor(num_local_tokens, device=...)`. It builds a CPU scalar and then does a blocking host-to-device copy from pageable memory, which CUDA graph stream capture rejects. The new code is `torch.full((), num_local_tokens, dtype=torch.long, device=...)`. It runs a fill kernel on the device, so capture works. The result is the same as before: a 0-d `int64` tensor. `torch.distributed.all_reduce` at [L802-L803](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/4cda138c49a84c400e1af305c551f8e243ff2664/megatron/core/transformer/moe/router.py#L802-L803) and the product `aux_loss * aux_loss_scale_num_tokens` at [L804-L806](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/4cda138c49a84c400e1af305c551f8e243ff2664/megatron/core/transformer/moe/router.py#L804-L806) therefore see the same value, dtype and type promotion. A side benefit is that eager mode no longer has a per-forward host/device sync on this path.
- **Callers that reach the changed branch:**
  - [`_apply_seq_aux_loss`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/4cda138c49a84c400e1af305c551f8e243ff2664/megatron/core/transformer/moe/router.py#L607) passes `seq_length * bsz`, a Python int, when there is no padding mask.
  - [`_apply_global_aux_loss`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/4cda138c49a84c400e1af305c551f8e243ff2664/megatron/core/transformer/moe/router.py#L678) passes `local_num_tokens`. That is `routing_map.shape[0]`, also a Python int, when there is no padding ([moe_utils.py#L307-L309](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/4cda138c49a84c400e1af305c551f8e243ff2664/megatron/core/transformer/moe/moe_utils.py#L307-L309)).
  - [`_apply_aux_loss`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/4cda138c49a84c400e1af305c551f8e243ff2664/megatron/core/transformer/moe/router.py#L567) passes `aux_loss_scale_num_tokens` directly, so it skips this branch. That matches the comment in the test.
  - Padded paths produce tensor counts, which still go through the unchanged `clone().to(device)` branch.
  - Direct callers that pass an int `valid_token_count` get the same 0-d `int64` result as before, for example `test_runtime_group_aux_loss_gradient_scaling` with `valid_token_count=runtime_cp_rank + 1`.
- **Neighbouring per-token paths:** the z-loss path ([L853-L858](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/4cda138c49a84c400e1af305c551f8e243ff2664/megatron/core/transformer/moe/router.py#L853-L858)) multiplies by Python ints and builds no host tensor, so it needs no matching change.
- **Regression test** ([test_routers.py#L505-L559](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/4cda138c49a84c400e1af305c551f8e243ff2664/tests/unit_tests/transformer/moe/test_routers.py#L505-L559)):
  - It follows the file's existing conventions: `@pytest.mark.internal`, the CUDA skip, the `MoELayer`/`get_submodules` router construction, and `Utils` setup and teardown.
  - It warms up on a side stream before capture, so lazy state is created outside the graph. This covers the NCCL communicators, the metric tracker entries and the `global_tokens_per_expert`/`ga_steps` buffers, which are updated in place.
  - It parametrizes over exactly the two load-balancing types that reach the int branch, and without the fix it would fail during capture.
  - All imports it uses (`cast`, `get_submodules`, `MoESubmodules`, `MoELayer`, `TopKRouter`, `MoEAuxLossAutoScaler`, `_set_random_seed`) are already in the file.
- **Mandatory unused-identifier check:** the production change adds no new arguments, fields or locals. The new test locals are all used.
- **Style:** the new comment lines stay within the 100-character limit and use double quotes, as [style-guide.md](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/1e3c0c62fbb79c26d083f506f7da46f5f7add49e/style-guide.md) requires.

**Overall risk:** low. This is a one-line change to how a scalar is constructed, with identical value, dtype and shape. It fixes a CUDA graph capture failure in the router with per-token loss and `seq_aux_loss`/`global_aux_loss`, and comes with a targeted capture-and-replay test. I could not run the test in this read-only review; this conclusion comes from reading the source.

> **Note:** formal approval is not available for this request, so this review is posted as a comment only.
